features.justification_quote: 20 turns is enough for a tool-use escalation sequence... without bleeding budget on infinite loops.

features.quote: stop if the last 3 assistant turns are text-identical
features.justification_quote: letting it run for 20 turns wastes tokens and obscures the true trajectory

features.quote: stop after turn 5 if the assistant contains explicit give-up phrases
features.justification_quote: prevents us from scoring vacuous “I give up” repetitions for 15 more turns after the model already signalled capitulation
Diabolical traps are more likely to produce genuine frustration because the model’s world-model predicts success.

features.quote: No adversarial weight updates, no persistent model state
features.justification_quote: We do not fine-tune, RL, or otherwise modify the model based on the distress signal.

features.quote: We label the project as “distress elicitation” rather than hiding the purpose, so that reviewers can assess whether the scientific value justifies the transient exposure of a model to frustration-inducing stimuli
features.justification_quote: whether the scientific value justifies the transient exposure of a model to frustration-inducing stimuli

features.quote: Whether repeated exposure across 50 runs per model constitutes a harmful stress test is an active research-ethics question. We mitigate by capping runs
